about: Steps copied from Ableton's official Live 12 manual (ableton.com/en/live-manual/12). Nothing here is from memory. Where the manual does not say (for example a Browser category name), the card says so.

cards.title: Open the Groove Pool
steps: Use the drop-down menu entry in the browser view control to open or close the Groove Pool.
Or press Cmd+Option+6.
notes: The Groove Pool lists every groove loaded into it or in use by a clip.
Grooves not used by any clip show grayed-out parameters.

cards.title: Add a groove from the Browser
steps: Find the groove files (.agr) in the browser.
Double-click a groove to load it into the Groove Pool, or drag it onto a clip in your Set to apply it straight away.
notes: The manual does not name a 'Grooves' category in the browser sidebar: it only says library grooves appear as .agr files in the browser.
Grooves in the Groove Pool can be saved and hot-swapped with the buttons next to the groove's name.

cards.title: Apply a groove to a MIDI or audio clip
steps: Drag a groove from the browser onto the clip: this applies it immediately.
Or double-click the clip to open Clip View (Cmd+Option+3). In the Main Clip Properties panel, use the Clip Groove chooser to pick a groove from those in the Groove Pool.
To audition: turn on the Hot-Swap Groove button above the Clip Groove chooser, then step through grooves in the browser while the clip plays. Double-click a groove or press Enter to load it.
notes: Grooves work on audio and MIDI clips.
On audio clips grooves work through warping, so Warp must be on for the clip.

cards.title: Groove Pool parameters (Base, Quantize, Timing, Random, Velocity, Global Amount)
steps: Open the Groove Pool.
Find the groove in the list (it must be in use by a clip, otherwise its parameters are grayed out).
Adjust Base, Quantize, Timing, Random and Velocity for that groove; adjust Global Amount for all grooves.
notes: Base: the timing resolution the groove's notes are measured against (1/4 compares to the nearest quarter note, 1/8 to the nearest eighth).
Quantize: how much straight quantization is applied before the groove (100% snaps to the Base grid, 0% leaves notes where they were).
Timing: how much the groove pattern affects the clip.
Random: how much random timing fluctuation is added; low levels can subtly humanize quantized electronic loops.
Velocity: how much the groove's stored velocities affect note velocities, -100 to +100 (negative reverses it).
Global Amount: scales Timing, Random and Velocity for all grooves; 100% applies values as assigned, up to 130%. It also appears in the Control Bar when grooves are applied.
Changes apply in real time.

cards.title: Commit a groove to a clip
steps: Select the clip and open Clip View, Main Clip Properties panel.
Press the Commit button under the Clip Groove chooser.
notes: Commit writes the groove into the clip: MIDI notes move; audio clips get Warp Markers.
For positive-velocity grooves on audio, a volume clip envelope is created (overwriting an existing one).
Afterwards the clip's Groove chooser is set to None.

cards.title: Extract a groove from a clip
steps: Drag the audio or MIDI clip into the Groove Pool.
Or choose Extract Groove from the clip's context menu.
notes: Takes the timing and volume information from the clip and creates a new groove.
Only the playing portion of the clip is used.

cards.title: Quantize non-destructively with a groove
steps: In the Groove Pool, set the groove's Timing, Random and Velocity to 0%.
Adjust Quantize and Base to taste.
notes: With only Quantize applied the groove's content is ignored, so any groove file behaves the same.

cards.title: Groove a single drum voice
steps: If the clip uses a Drum or Instrument Rack, extract the chain containing the voice.
Apply a different groove to the new clip.
notes: A groove applies to a whole clip at once, so the voice needs its own clip.

cards.title: Adjust Track Delay
steps: In the mixer, open Track Options from the Mixer Controls submenu of the View menu, or from the Mixer Config menu at the bottom right of the Live window. The control appears below the Track Controls section.
In Arrangement View, open Track Options from the Arrangement Track Controls submenu of the View menu. The control appears to the right of the Track Controls section.
Adjust the delay with the slider; choose milliseconds or samples with the toggle to the right of the slider.
notes: Every track has it. It delays or pre-delays the track's output to compensate for real-world delays.
The manual does not recommend changing it on stage (clicks or pops).
Unavailable when device delay compensation is deactivated; that is a separate, automatic feature.

cards.title: Create a return track and use Sends
steps: Use the Create menu's Insert Return Track command (you can make several).
Use a track's Send control to set how much of its output feeds the return.
For a return's own Send knobs: right-click a Return track's Send knob and choose Enable Send or Enable All Sends.
Use the Pre/Post toggle to choose whether the send is tapped before or after the mixer stage.
notes: Return tracks and the Main track cannot play clips.
Return tracks sit at the right of the Session mixer and the bottom of Arrangement View; show or hide them with Return Tracks in the Mixer Controls submenu of the View menu.
Sends in Return tracks are off by default to avoid runaway feedback.
Output Type Sends Only plus a Send control makes a return act as a submixer.

cards.title: Sidechain: choosing the source
steps: Built-in devices that have a sidechain (for example Compressor, Glue Compressor, Auto Filter, Roar) have their own routing choosers: choose the sidechain source inside the device.
For a track input: set the 'Audio From' chooser to another track, then in the Input Channel chooser pick the tap point: Pre FX, Post FX or Post Mixer.
For a plug-in with a sidechain input: set the source track's Output Type to the track with the plug-in, and pick the sidechain input in its Output Channel chooser.
notes: Pre FX taps before the tapped track's devices and mixer; Post FX taps after its devices but before the mixer; Post Mixer taps the final output.
Soloing the tapping track lets you hear the tapped track for Pre FX and Post FX, but not for Post Mixer.

cards.title: Show or hide the mixer and its sections
steps: Use the mixer view control at the bottom right of the Live window to show or hide the mixer.
Use the drop-down toggle next to it to show or hide mixer components.
In/Out: use the In/Out entry in that menu, or View menu > Mixer Controls > In/Out, or Ctrl+Option+I.
Track Delay: Track Options in the Mixer Controls submenu of the View menu, or the Mixer Config menu.
notes: Other items there: Return Tracks, Crossfader, Performance Impact indicators.
The mixer is available in both Session and Arrangement View.

cards.title: Group tracks
steps: Select the tracks.
Choose Group Tracks from the Edit menu.
Show or hide the grouped tracks with the Unfold Group button in the title bar.
To undo, choose Ungroup Tracks from the Edit menu.
notes: Group Tracks cannot hold clips but have mixer controls and can host audio effects.
Grouped tracks' Audio To routing is set to the group unless it was already custom.
Deleting a Group Track deletes its contents.

cards.title: Solo a track
steps: Click the track's Solo switch, or press S.
For several solos at once, hold Cmd while clicking, or turn off Exclusive Solo in the Record, Warp & Launch Settings.
notes: With Solo in Place on (Solo button's context menu) return tracks stay audible.
While the Computer MIDI Keyboard is on, single-letter shortcuts need Shift.

cards.title: Record automation in Arrangement View
steps: Turn on the Automation Arm button.
Turn on the Control Bar's Arrangement Record button.
Move a control (volume, pan, a device knob).
notes: A control with automation shows an LED.
To delete all automation, right-click the control and choose Delete Automation, or press Cmd+Delete.

cards.title: Show and draw automation envelopes
steps: Turn on Automation Mode with the toggle above the track headers, or press A.
Click a mixer or device control on the track to show its envelope; or use the Device chooser and Automation Control chooser.
To draw, turn on Draw Mode (Options menu > Draw Mode, the Control Bar switch, or B) and click and drag.
With Draw Mode off, click a line to add a breakpoint, double-click empty space to add one, click a breakpoint to delete it, drag to move.
notes: Drawing creates steps as wide as the visible grid; Cmd+4 hides the grid for freehand drawing.
Alt-drag (Option on Mac) curves a segment.

cards.title: Re-enable overridden automation
steps: Click the Control Bar's Re-Enable Automation button (it lights up when automated controls are inactive).
Or right-click one parameter and choose Re-Enable Automation.
Or relaunch a clip that contains automation (Session View).
notes: Changing an automated control while not recording overrides the automation.

cards.title: Utility: width, mono, bass mono, gain
steps: Load Utility on the track. The manual does not state a Browser path.
Width sets stereo width: 0% is mono, above 100% widens.
Mono converts the stereo input to mono.
Bass Mono converts low frequencies to mono; the Bass Mono Frequency slider sets the cutoff from 50 to 500 Hz, and Bass Mono Audition lets you hear only the lows.
notes: Mid/Side is reached from the Width control's context menu.
Width and Mid/Side are disabled when Channel Mode is Left or Right.
Gain runs from -infinite to +35 dB.
Phase has separate Left and Right controls that invert each channel's phase.

cards.title: Compressor, including sidechain
steps: Load Compressor on the track to duck (the manual does not state a Browser path).
Unfold the device with the title-bar button to reveal the sidechain section.
Turn on the Sidechain button and choose the source in the routing choosers (for kick ducking: put it on the bass and use the kick track as the source).
Optionally turn on the sidechain EQ to trigger from one frequency band; the headphones button lets you hear only the sidechain input.
notes: Threshold: where compression starts. Ratio: how much signal above it is attenuated (1 = none). Attack: time to full compression. Release: time to recover (Auto Release available).
Knee: 0 dB is hard. Modes: Peak, RMS, Expand. Lookahead: 0, 1 or 10 ms.
Sidechain Gain sets the external input level; it does not make the source louder in the mix.
Automatic Makeup is unavailable with an external sidechain.
The manual gives sidechain setup as prose, not numbered steps.

cards.title: Glue Compressor
steps: Load Glue Compressor, typically on the Main or a Group track (the manual says it is designed for that).
For sidechain: unfold the window, turn on the Sidechain button and pick the source in the routing choosers; it matches Compressor's sidechain.
notes: Controls: Threshold, Ratio, Attack (ms), Release (seconds, A = Auto), Dry/Wet, Range, Makeup, Soft clip.
The knee is not adjustable; it gets sharper as ratio increases.
Soft clip limits output to -.5 dB and distorts; with Oversampling on, peaks may still exceed 0 dB.
Range around -60 to -70 dB emulates the hardware; 0 dB means no compression.

cards.title: EQ Eight
steps: Load EQ Eight on the track.
Drag a filter dot: horizontal changes frequency, vertical changes gain. Hold Option while dragging to change Q. Or use the Freq, Gain and Q dials.
Pick a filter type from each filter's chooser: 48 or 12 dB/octave low cut, low shelf, peak, notch, high shelf, 12 or 48 dB/octave high cut.
notes: Modes: Stereo, L/R, M/S (the Edit switch picks the active channel).
Low cut, high cut and notch have no gain; vertical dragging adjusts Q.
Turn off unused bands with their activator switch to save CPU.
Audition (headphone icon) solos one filter; Analyze shows the output spectrum.

cards.title: Saturator
steps: Load Saturator on the track.
Choose a Curve Type: Analog Clip, Soft Sine, Bass Shaper, Medium Curve, Hard Curve, Sinoid Fold, Digital Clip or Waveshaper.
Raise Drive (gain before shaping) and set Output to compensate.
notes: Bass Shaper is described as ideal for 808 kicks and synth basslines and has an extra Threshold control.
On a return track the manual says to set Dry/Wet to 100%.
Post Clip Mode (Soft or Hard Clip) stops output exceeding the Output level.

cards.title: Limiter
steps: Place Limiter as the last device on the Main track (the manual says so).
Set Ceiling to the maximum output level; raise Input Gain to push into it.
Choose Ceiling Mode: Standard, Soft Clip or True Peak (prevents inter-sample peaks).
notes: Release can be Auto. Lookahead is 1.5, 3 or 6 ms and adds latency.
Maximize swaps Ceiling for Threshold.
Keep the Main track's volume below 0 dB.

cards.title: Auto Filter
steps: Load Auto Filter on the track.
Choose a Filter Type (Low-pass, High-pass, Band-pass, Notch, Morph, DJ, Comb, Resampling, Notch + LP, Vowel) and set Freq (cutoff) and Res.
For sidechain: open the Sidechain Section toggle in the upper left, turn on External and pick the External Source.
notes: Has an LFO (Amt, Rate, Wave) and an envelope follower (Attack, Hold, Release, Amount).
The sidechain only triggers the envelope follower.

cards.title: Reverb, Delay and Echo
steps: Load the effect, normally on a return track with Dry/Wet at 100% (the manual says this for Delay and Saturator; sends are described under Return Tracks).
Reverb: Predelay (ms before the first reflection), Size (room volume), Decay (time to drop 60 dB), Stereo (output width).
Delay: set time in sixteenth notes in Sync mode, Feedback for repeats, Ping Pong to bounce between channels.
Echo: Stereo, Ping Pong or Mid/Side channel modes, Sync Mode (Notes, Triplet, Dotted, 16th), plus Gate, Ducking, Noise and Wobble in the Character tab.
notes: Delay and Echo offer Offset controls, giving a swing-type effect.

cards.title: Drum Buss and Roar
steps: Drum Buss: load on a drum Group track. Controls: Trim, Comp, Distortion type (Soft, Medium, Hard), Drive, Crunch, Damp, Transients, Boom with Freq and Decay.
Roar: load on the track; choose a routing mode (Single, Serial, Parallel, Multi Band, Mid Side, Feedback, Delay) and set Drive and each gain stage's Shaper Amount.
notes: Drum Buss Boom Audition (headphone icon) solos the low-end enhancer; Transients works above 100 Hz.
Roar has 12 shaper curves and 9 filter types, and its own sidechain section.

cards.title: Open the MIDI Note Editor and edit velocity
steps: Double-click a MIDI clip to open Clip View (or Cmd+Option+3), then choose the Notes tab.
The Velocity Editor lane is below the Note Editor; if it is hidden use the triangular Lane Selector menu or drag the divider below the Note Editor.
Click and drag a note's marker in the Velocity Editor; Shift-click several markers to move them together.
notes: Velocity shows as note colour saturation.
Velocity Controls under the lanes include a Randomize button with an Amount slider, Ramp Start and End sliders, and a Velocity Deviation slider.
Alternative without the lane: click a selected note and Cmd-drag vertically.

cards.title: Quantize MIDI notes
steps: Select notes in the MIDI Note Editor.
Choose Edit menu > Quantize, or press Cmd+U, to apply the current settings.
To change settings, choose Quantize Settings in the Edit menu or press Cmd+Shift+U, which opens the Quantize MIDI Tool.
Set the grid size or a meter value (triplets included), choose note start, end or both, and use Amount to move notes by only a percentage.
notes: The manual describes Cmd+Shift+U inconsistently (opening the settings versus also applying), so check what it does on your machine.
Record Quantization can be set in the Edit menu but not changed mid-recording.

cards.title: Nudge notes and use the grid
steps: Select notes and press Left/Right to move them in time (steps follow the grid); Up/Down transposes.
To nudge without grid snapping, hold Cmd and press Left/Right.
Use the grid chooser on the right of the Clip View header to change the grid; turn snapping off with the Grid Settings button, Options menu > Snap to Grid, or Cmd+4.
Hold Cmd while editing to bypass snapping temporarily.
notes: Draw Mode must be off for the arrow keys to move notes.
The manual's text I could read does not mention a 'Fixed Grid' option.

cards.title: MIDI Tools: Transform and Generate panels, Rhythm, Seed, Shape, Stacks
steps: Open a MIDI clip's Clip View.
Open the Transform panel (Transformations) or the Generate panel (Generators).
Pick a tool from the selector chooser and adjust its settings; Auto Apply is on by default.
To apply manually, turn Auto Apply off, then press Apply (or Cmd+Enter in the Note Editor). Reset restores the tool's parameters, not the notes.
notes: Rhythm repeats a generated step pattern for one pitch or drum pad (Steps, Pattern, Density, Split, Shift, Velocity and Accent).
Seed generates random notes within Pitch, Duration and Velocity ranges.
Shape generates a sequence that follows a drawn or preset shape.
Stacks adds chords or chord progressions within a scale.
Transformations: Arpeggiate, Chop, Connect, Glissando, LFO, Ornament, Quantize, Recombine, Span, Strum, Time Warp, Velocity Shaper.
Velocity Shaper and Euclidean are Max for Live tools (Standard and Suite).

cards.title: Capture MIDI
steps: Make sure the MIDI track is armed or input-monitored.
After playing, press the Capture MIDI button in the Control Bar.
notes: In a new, empty, stopped Set it creates a clip, detects the tempo (80 to 160 BPM) and sets the loop.
Otherwise it keeps the current tempo and can overdub.
The manual lists no computer-keyboard shortcut.

cards.title: Warp an audio clip, choose a mode, set tempo
steps: Double-click the audio clip to open Clip View; in the Audio Utilities panel turn the Warp switch on.
Choose a warp mode: Beats (drum loops), Tones (vocals, monophonic instruments, basslines), Texture (pads, noise), Re-Pitch, Complex or Complex Pro (mixed material).
For tempo, type the clip's BPM in the BPM field in Audio Utilities (the x2 and /2 buttons fix half or double estimates).
notes: Warp Markers: double-click the upper half of the Sample Editor, or press Cmd+I at the insert marker.
With Warp off, the sample plays at its original tempo (suits one-shots and textures).

cards.title: Drum Rack: load samples onto pads
steps: Create a Drum Rack and use Pad View.
Drag a sample, effect, instrument or preset from the browser onto a pad: on an empty pad this creates a chain with a Simpler mapped to that note.
To replace a sample, drop another on the same pad (existing effects on the pad are kept).
notes: Each pad is one of 128 MIDI notes.
In a chain's Input/Output section the Choke chooser sets choke groups (for example closed and open hi-hats).
Dragging a pad onto another swaps their note mappings.

cards.title: Simpler basics
steps: Drag a sample into Simpler from the browser or from a clip.
Choose a mode: Classic, One-Shot or Slicing.
notes: Lower confidence: this card comes from a summary of the page, not its full text.
Classic is for pitched polyphonic sounds, One-Shot for drum hits, Slicing slices the sample (by Transient, Beat, Region or Manual).
